author: CC
prose: An outline check only stands for the documents it read. The BUILDME lane buildme_rides_the_outline_check accepts any ran:True record under outline_checks/<ticket>-*.json, but the record carries outline_sha256 and ticket_sha256 and nothing compares them to what stands now. Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendelllinux: ac71d984ebda's check (20261114T012013) was taken before outline commits 66c17d5a6 and 198f4ef24 (9.4.2.3.7 test tiers) and still crossed BUILDME; 207c4074b3d5's check predates a change to its falsifier and decisions. The opposite failure also happened: the integrator's walk re-ran outlinecheck on every walk, and each re-run opened new questions (2a20 gained open-c64761fc30c3, which cites 9.4.2.3.7.1, the outline line added after its earlier check). The orchestrator's rule: keep a ran:True check only if neither the ticket nor the outline changed since it ran; otherwise re-run. Today that rule lives only in the integrator's scratch script (/tmp/akienasus_ocfresh.py on the Dell). It belongs in the outline_check machine (reuse a fresh standing record, re-run a stale one) and in the sieve (red a stale record), with 'ticket changed' meaning its plan fields changed, not its cursor.
